newsitem.title: USA: Welfare reform could hurt Calif. counties - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Welfare reform could hurt Calif. counties - Moody's.

text.p: Federal welfare reform programs could hurt California counties unless policymakers reconsider safety net funding arrangements, Moody's Investors Service Inc said Friday.

"California, often the national trendsetter for municipal finance, will likely set the precedence for the nation's counties, as welfare reform begins to play out throughout all 50 states," Moody's analyst Renee Boicourt said.
Moody's said the projected cuts made by replacing Aid to Families with Dependent Children with a new block grant will not be very significant in a healthy economy.
But the program is not designed to expand much during recession, Moody's warned.

"The new program is clearly not designed to deal with an entitlement-style spike in demand, leaving the question of how states and localities will meet this need without increased recession-related fiscal stress," Moody's said.

California counties have historically borne the brunt of attempts at program reform, the rating agency said. The evolution of welfare reform in California will depend on actions not yet taken by its legislature, Moody's added.
"Counties will most likely feel the impact of reform policy," said Moody's analyst Ken Kurtz. "Los Angeles County will face the largest problems."
